q: When is the best time to visit Serengeti National Park?
a: Year-round wildlife is excellent in central Serengeti. Choose January–March for southern calving, May–June for western Grumeti action, and July–October for northern Mara River crossings. Dry months also mean clearer roads and classic game viewing.

q: How many days should I spend in the Serengeti?
a: Plan at least 3 nights for a meaningful taste; 4–5 nights if migration is your focus. Most strong northern-circuit trips place Serengeti inside a 7–9 day safari from Arusha.

q: Where should I stay for the Great Migration?
a: Match camp region to the month: Ndutu / south for calving, western corridor for Grumeti, north for Mara crossings, and Seronera as a reliable predator base when herds are elsewhere. Our Team adjusts as herds move.

q: Is a balloon safari worth it?
a: For many guests, yes — sunrise over the plains is unforgettable. Balloons are weather- and season-dependent and add a significant optional cost; we include availability checks on request.

q: Can I combine Serengeti with Ngorongoro and Zanzibar?
a: Yes — that is our most requested formula. Crater day + Serengeti nights, then fly or connect to Zanzibar beach. See our safari packages or request a custom quote.
